Blust (2013) only: voiceless palatal affricate [c͡ç] (Table 2.8, p. 30), in four PAn reconstructions (lecik, pacek, peceq, qapucuk). Other systems: Shibata does not treat it as a PAn phoneme, since Amis, Puyuma and Paiwan reflect it exactly as s and its distribution in western Indonesia can be explained by borrowing (pp. 31, 49); Ross (2015) finds it too weakly supported (p. 39); it is absent from the tables for Ross (1992) and Wolff (2010). Wolff's own symbol c stands for Blust's s. Phonetic value left blank in the chart, which follows Shibata. Blust (2013), quoted from Shibata (2025: 31).
